primary_source.title: Selmer groups and the indivisibility of Heegner points
primary_source.author: Wei Zhang
selectors: proof of Theorem 1.4(ii) and Remarks 2-3, p.8
verified_claims: Under Theorem 1.1's generalized-Heegner, residual-surjectivity, ramification and good-ordinary hypotheses, some derived Heegner class is nonzero, hence the Kolyvagin system is nonzero.
Theorem 1.2 identifies the Kolyvagin-system vanishing order with max of the two p-infinity Selmer eigencoranks over the auxiliary imaginary quadratic field minus one.

Theorem 1.4(ii) states that, for E/Q and p satisfying its four hypotheses, analytic rank greater than one implies Z_p-corank Sel_{p^infinity}(E/Q) at least two for root number +1 and at least three for root number -1.
For exact complex analytic rank two, functional-equation parity forces root number +1, so Theorem 1.4(ii) yields the scoped stored transfer ord_{s=1} L(E,s)=2 -> corank_Zp Sel_{p^infinity}(E/Q) >= 2.

In the proof of Theorem 1.4(ii), the auxiliary twist is chosen with nonzero first derivative in the root-number +1 case; Gross-Zagier then makes the base Heegner point torsion, giving only Kolyvagin-system vanishing order >=1 before Theorem 1.2 supplies the Selmer lower bound.
Remark 3 states that the set of primes satisfying Theorem 1.4(1)-(4) has density one for a fixed E/Q.
strict_nonclaims: The theorem does not prove exact Selmer corank two from exact complex analytic rank two.
The theorem does not prove a nonzero transverse localization at p; Remark 2 explicitly contrasts this method with Skinner's p-local surjectivity approach.
The theorem does not prove Mordell-Weil rank two, Sha finiteness, regulator nondegeneracy, or the full rank-two BSD leading-term formula.
The theorem is a technical-prime cell, not a theorem simultaneously at every prime p.
